title: A Better Library Experience | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our Library Window in CLO 2025.0 allows you to effortlessly transfer your previous favorites and manage custom libraries by renaming folders. Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

summary: ```markdown # A Better Library Experience | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have some great updates to share with you about our library, which has been improved in our release of 2025.0. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Library Location and Layout First, I'm just going to draw all of your attention to where the new library is. It is now located at the top right of your screen. It's represented by an icon with three lines connecting. When you click it, your library will pop up. There will still be a keyboard shortcut to open and close it, which is shortcut Y. We decided to make it a pop-up to give you more screen space so that your 2D and 3D windows can be larger than before. That's the whole point of moving it to the side—especially on smaller screens, you have more space to work with. If you absolutely hate this new setup, guess what? You can always revert back. By clicking the back button, a prompt will appear asking if you want to proceed with reverting to the previous library. If you are ready for new things and want to try the new library, you can switch to it by selecting “switch to new library” at the bottom. This allows you to try it out, learn more, or cancel. If you hit "learn more," a manual page will pop up and walk you through everything about the new library. ## New Library Features Here it is! If you move the library around and then hit the number one on your keyboard, it will return to exactly where you last left it. This is particularly useful if you're using multiple screens and accidentally leave it on the wrong screen. You can always hit the little reset layout button at the bottom right to reset it. You can use shortcut Y again to bring the library in and out, or simply click the icon to toggle it. You also have the option to hit exit to close it. ### Library Layout Breakdown At the very top of the library are all of your libraries: - **Clo**: This contains all of your Clo assets. - **Clo Set**: This includes all of your Clo Set libraries and access. - **Your Own Library**: If you bring in your own folders using the add button, you can access any other folders on your desktop here. On the far left, you will see a breakdown of what's in each library. For the Clo library, you will see all of the Clo assets. For Clo Set, there is a breakdown of how Clo Set is organized, allowing you to browse through workspaces and favorites. ### Navigational Features The second level of the top section allows you to switch between your Clo assets and Connect assets easily. You can also use the search bar to look for items within any of these libraries. The third level shows you your current location in the library. For example, if you’re in garments, it will display that. This section also allows you to adjust how you want to view the items. ### Customizing Your View If you set your view preferences, they will be saved. For instance, if you like to see information in a certain way, it will automatically display that way when you return. There’s also a refresh button at the bottom for quickly updating your folders if you add something new. ## How the Library Works Now that we know the layout, let's discuss how it works. In the old library, folders marked as favorites are easily identifiable. When you hit add, it brings that folder into your favorites. Switching to the new library, you will see all of your CLO assets at the top, including everything preloaded into CLO. If you need to access CLOSET, you can log in through the user account option. ### Adding and Managing Libraries You can add new libraries by hitting the add button and creating new libraries. You can also transfer your previous favorites into the new library. You can rename folders by right-clicking and also delete them as needed. ### Organizing Your Assets The core assets like garments, avatars, fabrics, trims, and stages are all available on the left side. You can switch between Clo assets and Connect assets in the Clo library by clicking the Connect assets option. From there, you can search for specific items like jackets and organize them accordingly. ## Downloading Assets To download assets, you can check the items you want and download them all at once. You can also sort the assets by different criteria such as name, last modified, or type. You have the option to view items in icon format or detailed view, and there’s a preview panel that allows you to see the front, back, and side of garments. ### Dragging and Dropping Assets Dragging and dropping assets into your workspace is straightforward. If you want to add an asset, the pop-up will ask if you want to open or add it. You can right-click to add items to your workspace or copy paths, show in explorer, or open previous versions. The ability to manage your assets efficiently is a key feature of the new library. ## Creating Scenes The new library makes it incredibly easy to create and add items to your scene. For instance, you can bring in a file from Clo Set with just a drag and drop. You can also explore the Connect Store for additional items like stages, which enhances your creative possibilities. ## Conclusion Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe, and check out all of our great videos on our YouTube channel. There are many valuable resources for you to learn from. Keep having fun with CLO! ```
